text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- A recent report shows that Norwegian children spend too little time outdoors and spend too much time watching television instead. Researchers also are worried thatparents spend far too little time playing outdoors with their children
- Head of Norway's Supreme Court, Carsten Smith, has criticised the government for being one of the last to implement the European convention for human rights.
- Shareholders in Norway's largest insurer Storebrand and commercial bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse will vote today over the proposed merger between the two companies.

- State-owned oil company Statoil has decided to support the proposed merger between Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse. Statoil holds 0.4 percent of the shares in Storebrand and 0.5 percent of the shares in Christiania Bank.

- Labour Party member of parliament, Annelise Doerum, advises customers in both Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse to open accounts in other financial institutions if the proposed merger between the two goes through. Doerum is afraid that the merged finance giant will get too much power in the financial market.

- Anglo-Dutch oil company Shell could lose as much as 100 million crowns from operations in Norway. In the autumn the company will decide whether it will open unstaffed stations in order to reduce losses in the Norwegian market.
